source.title: Understanding Deep Learning: Expected Spanning Dimension and Controlling the Flexibility of Neural Networks
source.authors: D. Berthiaume; R. Paffenroth; Lei Guo

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures expected spanning dimension and reports its association with training or test performance, and compares architectures with different ESD. These are related tests of flexibility and generalization, but do not directly test any listed version’s specified intervention or measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on fitting random noise, Fashion MNIST and CIFAR-10 performance, and ESD associations with ImageNet test error. The random-noise figure gives no numeric values; the text says only the add-inputs model fits the noise. ImageNet model-level ESD and error values are shown in figures, with aggregate associations described in text. ESD is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7, and the paper does not measure the train-test gap as specified by any version.
record.test_reason: Sections 5.1–5.2 test a component of V1: the same add-inputs architecture fits arbitrarily classified noise images and generalizes on structured images. This differs from randomizing labels on natural images and omits random-label held-out accuracy. ESD correlations and the remaining architecture comparisons do not test another version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that ESD measures network flexibility, that added links can increase ESD and improve training and test performance without increasing parameter count, and that ESD predicts ImageNet performance across the examined architectures. They leave unresolved whether improvement reflects underfitting or operation beyond a double-descent threshold.
record.recipe_differences: Measures Jacobian-based expected spanning dimension and modifies network links; it does not reproduce the listed interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: For ImageNet networks, the reported association differs with the output mapping (sum_squares is stronger than pick_1st) and with synthetic versus ImageNet inputs; ESD ranges are larger on ImageNet inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding input shortcuts improves training and test accuracy over the compared architectures at the reported epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input shortcuts can improve optimization and held-out performance in these image-classification experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: ESD correlates negatively with ImageNet test error across 18 architectures; parameter count has a weaker, nonsignificant linear association.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jacobian effective-rank-based architectural flexibility predicts held-out image-classification performance across the examined architectures.

record.peer_reviewed: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics
record.problems: The authors note that testing error is affected by training difficulty, learning-algorithm limitations, input structure and distribution, training-set size and outliers. The real-world ImageNet comparisons use torchvision-reported testing errors and ESD figures rather than reporting per-network numerical values in the text. ESD is an indirect measure and the reported association is correlational.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's per-network ESD and ImageNet test-error values in Figures 9–12 are figure-only; they are not individually transcribed. Additional p-values across mapping, error type, data type and removed-network subsets in Tables 3–4 are not individually rowed because the flattened table excerpt does not reliably preserve all condition-to-value associations.

untested.parts: Held-out accuracy under random labels; randomizing labels on otherwise unchanged natural images; exact near-perfect noise-fitting accuracy; matched training recipes and absence of explicit regularization. Structured-data identification is inconsistent between Figure 7 and Section 5.2/Table 1.
Test error under widening beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size changes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with train-test gaps, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing examples selected by label memorization versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: V1 is tested only through a different-method coexistence comparison, not a complete replication. Natural-data training rows provide context, while verdicts rest on noise-fitting results paired with held-out accuracy. ESD correlations do not test V2 or V7. The ImageNet errors are externally reported torchvision results; the study's own contribution is their association with computed ESD.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the same architectures and recipes on both fixed random labels and natural labels with held-out accuracy.
No width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold under the specified conditions.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on the listed image datasets or test the stated local-connectivity mechanism.
Measures ESD, not magnitude-aware sharpness or perturbation tolerance, and does not assess which measure ranks train-test gaps better.
No removal of memorized training examples.
